chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Isma'il ibn Marar from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from a man from Abu Basir who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who claimed the child of a woman for whom no father was known, then he disowned that claim. He said: 'He does not have that right.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ لَهُ ذَلِكَ: He does not have that right

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man claims a child is his and then later disowns it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *luhq* (attachment of lineage), ruling that a man who claims paternity of a child with an unknown father cannot later disown them to escape obligations. This establishes that paternity by declaration is binding and irrevocable in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring the child's rights to inheritance and maintenance are secured. The ruling underscores the stability of family structures and the seriousness of claiming lineage in Islamic law.
